value.body: A respiratory therapist looks after patients who have trouble breathing, especially in intensive care. Employers are mainly multi-specialty hospitals with ICUs, and some pulmonology clinics. A typical day involves checking and adjusting ventilator settings with the ICU team, giving nebulisation and oxygen therapy, and running lung function tests.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Graduates usually join hospital ICUs after an internship during the degree. Larger hospitals have dedicated respiratory therapy teams; in smaller ones the work may be shared with nurses and anaesthesia technologists.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working in ICU teams under pressure

value.title: At a glance
items: The role is better established in large city hospitals than in smaller towns.
Night shifts and ICU pressure are part of the job.
Next roles: senior therapist, respiratory care in-charge, educator.
